children.prompt: In the first diagram, state the area of triangle $ABC$.

children.prompt: In the second diagram, show that $\angle DGC$ is $2\theta$ and $DE=\sin 2\theta$.

answer.short:
$\angle DGC=2\theta$ and $DE=\sin 2\theta$.

Use the exterior angle of triangle $AGC$, then the sine ratio in right-angled triangle $DGE$.
answer.worked:
Since $A$, $G$ and $D$ are collinear, $\angle DGC$ is an exterior angle of triangle $AGC$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle DGC&=\angle GAC+\angle ACG\\\angle DGC&=\theta+\theta\\\angle DGC&=2\theta.\end{align*}$$
Since $E$ lies on $GC$, $\angle DGE=2\theta$. In right-angled triangle $DGE$, $GD=1$, so
$$\begin{align*}\sin 2\theta&=\frac{DE}{GD}\\\sin 2\theta&=\frac{DE}{1}\\DE&=\sin 2\theta.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin 2\theta$.

The diagonal $BC$ divides the rectangle into triangles of equal area.
answer.worked:
The diagonal $BC$ divides rectangle $ABDC$ into two triangles of equal area, so $\operatorname{Area}(ABC)=\operatorname{Area}(BCD)$. Using $BC=2$ and the perpendicular height $DE=\sin 2\theta$,
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(BCD)&=\frac12\times BC\times DE\\\operatorname{Area}(BCD)&=\frac12\times2\times\sin 2\theta\\\operatorname{Area}(BCD)&=\sin 2\theta.\end{align*}$$
Part a gives $\operatorname{Area}(ABC)=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$. Therefore
$$2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin 2\theta.$$
